elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant as rendered: "TrueLink hereby grants to Client, and to Client's affiliates upon written notice to TrueLink, a non-exclusive license to use the Interface". "Client" is defined in the preamble as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so the affiliate extension adds new coverage rather than duplicating it.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered grant names only Client and Client's affiliates; no language covers contractors or other third parties acting on Client's behalf. To meet this, the grant would need "and contractors acting on Client's behalf".
§ 2(c) retained unchanged: "The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12." No perpetual term for any paid-up licence is stated.
No "irrevocable" language appears anywhere in the rendered grant; the licence simply endures until termination under § 12, so it remains revocable on any § 12 termination ground.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: § 2(c) cross-refers termination to Section 12, but Section 12's grounds are not in the cited or rendered text, so it cannot be verified that termination is limited to uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: § 15 as rendered adds "or, in Client's case, a transfer of the license to a successor in a merger or acquisition", giving Client a no-consent licence transfer to a successor (limited to M&A successors, which is the fallback formulation but satisfies successor transferability in substance).

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted in § 2(a): "and to Client's affiliates upon written notice to TrueLink" — coverage is triggered by written notice exactly as the fallback requires, and no retained sentence contradicts it.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: § 15 exception as rendered: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, in Client's case, a transfer of the license to a successor in a merger or acquisition." The new exception is Client-only and does not create any new Vendor assignment right.

reasons: Both fallback elements are met in operative language: affiliate coverage on written notice inside the § 2(a) grant, and a Client-only no-consent licence transfer to an M&A successor in § 15. The fallback checklist is therefore position-complete and the deviation classification with a fallback-targeted redline is appropriate.

Preferred level is incomplete: no contractor coverage, no perpetual or irrevocable paid-up licence, and § 2(c) still ties the licence's life to termination under Section 12 whose grounds are not shown (so the uncured-material-breach-only limit cannot be verified). No repair is required if the fallback is the chosen target.

Minimality holds. Only two insertions were made, each traceable to a selected fallback element; § 2(a)'s Customer-favourable non-exclusivity/alternative-sourcing sentence and § 2(c) are untouched, and the retained mutual affiliate assignment exception is preserved rather than deleted (the ASSIGN fallback bar on non-successor exceptions is not part of this checklist). No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or other extras were added.

No duplicate coverage arises because "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so the affiliate extension is not redundant; and because a grant to an affiliate carries use through its authorised personnel, no separate personnel/access edit was (correctly) attempted.

The § 15 edit is drafted as a direct, narrowly scoped exception to the existing consent mechanic rather than a broad notwithstanding override, so the retained consent requirement is not contradicted and no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created; unrelated allocation, timing, and commercial mechanics survive intact.

Minor drafting nit (not a failure): in § 2(a) the field-of-use phrase "in the ordinary course of its business" now follows a two-party grant; the drafter may wish to render it "their respective businesses" for clarity, but as written it does not defeat any checklist element.
